sources.text:
10 wk summer placement, Brightwater Analytics (small fintech), Manchester, Jun-Aug 2026
team: me + 2 platform engineers (Mateo, Jen)
- goal: move the nightly risk batch jobs off one big VM onto EKS so they stop blocking each other
- stack: Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus, Loki
- decision: spot instances for the batch node pool, on-demand for the Argo controller. cheaper, jobs are retryable anyway
- problem: jobs randomly lost progress overnight, ~5% of runs. cause: spot interruptions + checkpoints only every 10 min
- investigated via node termination events in CloudWatch + the job logs. the 2 min warning wasn't enough
- fix: checkpoint every 90 s + a drain handler on the termination notice
- result: nightly run 4h10m -> 2h35m, nothing blocked since
- learned: read the spot termination docs first, not after
- why Graphcore: liked the scheduling side more than the models. want to work on the platform under the models
I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools and the Karpenter autoscaler config myself, and Mateo reviewed them.

documents.text:
During a ten-week summer placement at Brightwater Analytics in Manchester, our three-person platform team moved the nightly risk batch jobs from a single virtual machine onto EKS. The stack included Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus and Loki.

The decision was to use spot instances for the batch node pool and on-demand instances for the Argo controller, because that was cheaper and the jobs were retryable anyway.

About 5% of runs randomly lost progress overnight, with spot interruptions and checkpoints only every 10 minutes as the cause. Node termination events in CloudWatch and the job logs showed that the 2-minute warning was not enough. The fix was to checkpoint every 90 seconds and add a drain handler on the termination notice. The nightly run went from 4h10m to 2h35m, with nothing blocked since. The lesson was to read the spot termination documents first, not after.

The team consisted of me plus two platform engineers, Mateo and Jen. I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools, and Mateo wrote the Karpenter autoscaler config, which I reviewed. Mateo reviewed them.

Dear Graphcore hiring team,

I am applying for the Graduate Cloud Platform Engineer 2027 role at Graphcore.

I liked the scheduling side more than the models, and I want to work on the platform under the models.

A 10 wk summer placement at Brightwater Analytics in Manchester ran from Jun to Aug 2026. The team was me plus 2 platform engineers, Mateo and Jen. The goal was to move the nightly risk batch jobs off one big VM onto EKS so they stop blocking each other. I wrote the Terraform modules for the node pools, and Mateo wrote the Karpenter autoscaler config, which I reviewed. Mateo reviewed them. The stack included Terraform, EKS, Karpenter, Argo Workflows, Prometheus and Loki.

Spot instances were used for the batch node pool and on-demand instances for the Argo controller, because this was cheaper and the jobs are retryable. Jobs randomly lost progress overnight, ~5% of runs, due to spot interruptions and checkpoints only every 10 min. Node termination events in CloudWatch and the job logs were used to investigate, and the 2 min warning was not enough. The fix was a checkpoint every 90 s plus a drain handler on the termination notice. The nightly run went from 4h10m to 2h35m, with nothing blocked since. The lesson was to read the spot termination docs first, not after.

Thank you for considering my application.

Yours sincerely, Ellie
